# One-click-per-impression check in Redis

> A Redis SET NX on the impression ID with 1-hour expiry rejects repeat clicks on the same impression.

_Part of [Ad click tokens and fraud checks](ad-click-tracking-and-fraud.md)_

After [verifying the signed click token]([Signed click token with 30-minute expiry](click-token.md)), the click handler attempts a Redis SET NX on `adclick:{impression_id}` with 1-hour expiry. The SET succeeds only if the key doesn't already exist; success means this impression is being clicked for the first time in the 1-hour window, while failure means it's a repeat click. On repeat clicks, the handler returns immediately with the click marked `valid: false`. Duplicate impressions never reach [IP burst filtering]([Per-IP burst limit of 20 clicks a minute](ip-burst-filter.md)) or Kafka publishing. The user still gets redirected to the product page, preserving the browsing experience, but the click doesn't count toward billing or spend tracking.

**Look at:** [ads.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/ads.service.ts)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | ``adclick:{`impression_id`}`` | Redis key set to '1' with NX option and 3600-second expiry; SET NX fails (returns nil) if the key already exists, blocking the duplicate click immediately |

## Watch out

- Redis SET NX returns nil (falsy) when the key already exists, so the code negates it: `if (!set(...))` means the impression was a duplicate
- The 1-hour window is exact; repeat clicks are rejected only if they arrive within 3600 seconds of the first click, not based on wall-clock hours
- This is impression-level deduplication only: it doesn't care about IP, user, or campaign—it's purely 'was this exact impression ID clicked in the last hour?'
- Duplicate impressions never reach Kafka at all; the click method returns early, skipping Kafka publishing and spend counter increments entirely
